correctness.rationale: For every simultaneous eigenmode of the commuting graph Laplacian and force covariance, stationary moment balances give \(\mathbb E[vf]=s\tau/[m(1+\gamma\tau+\tau^2\lambda)]\), stationary kinetic variance \(T/m+s\tau/[m^2\gamma(1+\gamma\tau+\tau^2\lambda)]\), and the corresponding centered position variance for every positive frequency. The translation-projected linear dynamics are stable and yield a unique Gaussian stationary law. The spectral velocity covariance is flat if and only if \(\Sigma=c[(1+\gamma\tau)I+\tau^2 L]\), with \(c>0\). Gaussianity plus vanishing position–velocity covariance proves the two-temperature factorization and \(T_{\mathrm{conf}}-T_{\mathrm{kin}}=\tau J\). On the ring, the inverse of \(aI-bA\) is strictly positive entrywise by its convergent graph-walk expansion, so every off-diagonal covariance has the sign of \(1+a\varepsilon/b\), with a single zero strictly inside the assumed admissible interval. A direct full-dimensional stationary Lyapunov solver passed 80 parameterized cases with maximum observed discrepancy \(6.151\times10^{-14}\). Finite computational tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The source study asks how correlated active fluctuations organize velocity domains; controlling spatial forcing correlations to eliminate or reverse every pairwise covariance is a natural physical inverse problem. The theorem gives an exact graph-topology-independent matching criterion, simultaneously a nontrivial two-temperature Gibbs marginal and a strict positive dissipation witness, and a parameter-sharp negative/zero/positive sign diagram for all spatial separations on rings. It distinguishes instantaneous Gaussian independence from thermodynamic equilibrium. The covariance design is positive definite on every graph and corresponds to physically realizable edge-dipole active forcing. These structural and global classification statements go beyond a parameter substitution or tabulated recomputation.
